title: Security: on an environment kernel, a permission set saved through the metadata door keeps granting its old body until the kernel is rebuilt (applyRegistryWriteThrough skips environment-scoped writes; the security catalog reads the registry first)
body:
Filed by the `repo:cloud#1` seat (seat post #6026, session `session_01WVbr5J6u8BHh8EyFtcWciH`). Source: objectstack-ai/cloud#2869 `6148855560` (out-of-scope finding 1), measured in-process on a hosted tenant kernel at framework `01a3421f42`. **Security** (it could leak data). It also makes cloud's v18 upgrade need an extra kernel rebuild, so it is filed `priority:p1`, `target:v18`.

## What happens

- **The save is accepted:** on an environment kernel, `protocol.saveMetaItem({ type: 'permission', mode: 'publish' })` stores the new body, and `metadata.get` serves it.
- **The engine keeps the old body:** `ql.registry.getItem` still serves the boot-time body. The security catalog reads the registry first (`securityCatalogReaderOf`), so it keeps resolving the OLD permission set until the kernel is rebuilt.
- **Measured:**
  - the new body was `isDefault: true`, no `allowDelete`;
  - the registry kept `allowDelete: true`, no `isDefault`;
  - the catalog offered no `everyone` suggestion until a reboot.
- **No in-process refresh exists:** `protocol.loadMetaFromDb()` after boot answers `storeUnavailable: true`.
- **The same applies to an administrator** who narrows a permission set through `PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/NAME` on a tenant environment. The narrowed set keeps granting its old, wider body until the kernel is rebuilt.

## Where

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` `applyRegistryWriteThrough` (around line 19628) returns when `this.environmentId !== undefined`. The doc comment gives the reason: "a project-scoped row must not be registered into a registry that unscoped (control-plane) callers share". That holds for a shared registry. On a kernel that hydrates its own `sys_metadata` (`hydrateMetadataFromDb`, where each engine owns its registry), the same gate leaves the security-relevant registry stale.

## Ask

On a kernel whose registry is its own (not shared with unscoped callers), write a published permission body through to the registry, or otherwise make the catalog read the saved body. The lane decides the shape. ⛔ Not a cloud-side cache flush.

Cloud's migration (objectstack-ai/cloud#2869) works around the one-boot case by requesting an environment rebuild. With this fix it completes in one boot, with no cloud change.
